description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself. Closed out 2026-05-08; substrate-convergence work in analyses 026-030 + the Geocities showcase landed the "Tweedles don't ship" bug class. P7 evals deferred behind P8 (operator interface) so the eval harness has a usable surface to run against.

phases.title: Observer API
phases.notes: HistoricalRunHandle reads any captured snapshot directory — parses run.log, reads the per-agent SQLite databases, loads the telemetry JSON, exposes summary() / meetings() / utterances() / per_agent_telemetry() / artifacts(). The replay-side surface that everything else in P8 sits on. Shipped 2026-05-07 alongside P8.2.

phases.title: TUI Inspector
phases.notes: Textual-based read-only TUI: snapshot library, run summary, meeting detail with body preview + speaker filter + utterance modal, artifact browser (global + meeting-scoped, attribution via bus not mtime), cast view, theme cycling, app-wide vim navigation. First public release — wonderland-ai 0.0.1 on PyPI 2026-05-08.

phases.title: Streaming + Mock Turtle
phases.notes: Foundation for live-watch UX. Extend RunHandle with stream_events() async iterator; HistoricalRunHandle defaults to yield-now (no behavior change for inspector); MockTurtleHandle replays a snapshot's events with compressed timing + dwell cap so we iterate live-watch UI against a free testbed. After P8.3 the TUI can subscribe to "events as they arrive" without caring whether the source is replay, mock, or eventually a real bus.

phases.title: Live-watch screen
phases.notes: New LiveRunScreen that consumes the streaming API — meeting cells fill in as events arrive, current speaker indicator, live cost ticker, drill-down into in-progress meetings shows partial transcripts. Iterated entirely against Mock Turtle replay so zero API spend during UX iteration. The screen that turns Wonderland from "things happen and you read transcripts later" into "things happen and you watch them happen."

phases.title: Directive issuing + LiveRunHandle
phases.notes: NewRunScreen — directive textarea, workflow picker (TDD/canonical/smoke), project-root picker. LiveRunHandle wraps a real Runner+Caucus, emits via the same streaming API as MockTurtleHandle so the live-watch screen consumes both interchangeably. The leap from "replay testbed" to "actually launches a real run." First end-to-end test: directive → live watch → artifacts → done.

phases.title: New-project spinup (the rabbit hole)
phases.notes: Three entry paths converging on a single project-context capture: greenfield (skeleton picker + scaffold), existing-Wonderland (already covered by P8.5's project picker), adopt-existing (wonderland init + stack-detection routine that pre-fills the context form from manifest files). Persists .wonderland/project-context.md in a forward-compatible shape so future workflow-context injection has one input format to read. The on-ramp that turns "pip install" into "team's ready to start."

phases.title: First-use polish
phases.notes: Welcome/home screen (new run / browse snapshots / cast / configure), error states (missing API key, no project root, run failure), abort flow (clean shutdown of running threads), quiescence indicator (M5's long pauses need "still working, just thinking"), README + SHOWCASE updates with the TUI flow. The rough-edges sweep that closes the gap between "works for the developer" and "works for someone who just installed it."

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

phases.title: Meeting turns: phases + priority + rotations
phases.notes: Per analysis 033 (analyses/033-meeting-as-mtg-turn.md): lift phases + priority rotation + turns-as-budget from MtG into the meeting engine; skip the stack. Sequenced as a substrate phase that alternates with P8's interface track per the back-and-forth-stays-fresh rhythm. Engine work is bigger than P8's per-task shape and benefits from its own phase boundary. Engine + workflow schema + observer events are P1 (load-bearing); rotation counter + failure-mode detectors are P2 (instrumentation that lands once the structure exists).

phases.title: Two-Headed Giant: team windows
phases.notes: Per the live r35-tdd-serial-phased observation: strict-serial priority within a rotation imposes ~N× cast size wall-clock cost on constitutionally-paired agents (Tweedledee/Tweedledum, Alice/Hatter) who in legacy mode would have deliberated concurrently. Phase 9.5 generalizes phases by adding team_groupings: list[list[str]] per phase. A team window opens concurrently for all team members via asyncio.gather; structural cap preserved (rotation budget × team count = bounded deliberations); §VIII observability preserved (per-agent WindowOutcome unchanged). Maps onto MtG's Two-Headed Giant format — paired players take their team turn together. The natural design follow-up to P9; lands once analysis 034 quantifies the wall-clock penalty of the strict-serial baseline.

phases.title: Cost recovery: tool-call surfacing + diff-based writes
phases.notes: Per analyses 032 + 035: Tweedles are 78.8% of total run cost, with ~13-15 calls per deliberation reflecting heavy write_file → run_tests → write_file tool loops. Two batched fixes: (1) surface tool calls on the bus event log so post-run analysis can quantify exactly which tool calls drive cost (currently inferred via per-agent telemetry); (2) diff-based write tool that lets agents send deltas instead of full file contents, with analysis 032 estimating ~3.5× cost compression on iterative file authoring. Sequencing: surface first so we can measure baseline tool-call distribution; then diff tool with measurements to verify the predicted compression. After both ship, second pass to identify other easy cost/clock wins from whatever the surfaced data reveals.

phases.title: Polish: ambient liveness, first-use UX, small ergonomic improvements after P11
Feature lifecycle + workflow composability: split design / implement / verify; operator batching
Cross-run stability: make iterating tdd-design + tdd-implement against the same project the expected mode of operation
phases.notes: Most observed failure modes from multi-pass obol runs land as either 'everything completed at $0' (cross-run seeds re-emitted as fresh work) or duplicate artifacts (Rabbit revising mid-meeting, M2/M3 source-set sprawl). P12 shipped piecemeal patches (per-thread cost f36bbf7, exit_condition is_seed filter v0.3.2, consumed_by binding fb4fc0e); P13 closes the remaining gaps so cross-run iteration is the workflow's expected economic shape.

activePhase.title: Cross-run stability: make iterating tdd-design + tdd-implement against the same project the expected mode of operation
activePhase.goal: Close the cross-run stability gaps that emerged from running tdd-design + tdd-implement multiple times against a single project. Make cross-run iteration (5–10× design passes per project, partial implement runs, operator-driven re-queuing) the workflow's expected mode of operation rather than the surprise edge case the substrate has been treating it as. Operator should be able to wipe .wonderland/ and re-run, OR run a focused follow-on design pass (mock data, observability, etc.), without manually pruning duplicates or chasing 'everything completed at $0' diagnostics.
activePhase.sequencing: Layer 1 (foundation): T95 + T91 — substrate primitives that close the duplicate-emission and partial-run-state classes. T95 stops the bleeding at the source (M2/M3 don't ship duplicates anymore); T91 reconciles state when meetings abort or operators edit files outside the substrate. Layer 2 (observability): T96 — operator can see when API breaks (today's diagnosis was '$0 meetings' with no signal that the API was failing). Layer 3 (hardening): T97 + T98 — smaller polish that prevents specific drift classes. T97 closes the Cat-Flask-service drift door by adding process_model as an explicit project_context field; T98 distinguishes replay from live runs in the live-watch UI so the operator can't mistake a snapshot for in-flight work. Critical path: T95 first — duplicate emissions affect every other concern. T91 second — partial-run recovery requires lifecycle reconciliation. Then observability + polish in parallel.

tasks.title: Auto-dedup duplicate features/tickets at meeting close
tasks.details: Substrate-side fix for the M2/M3 revision-pass duplication observed twice in obol (May 10 mock-data design pass: M3 produced 36 tickets representing ~14 unique work atoms across 3 revision passes). Operator-side workaround shipped as the dashboard ticket-prune UI (commit e4ca7b5) but that's the band-aid; the substrate-side dedup is the real fix. Two coordinated changes: (1) iteration-time filter in _collect_per_item_items dedupes by (kind, frozenset(sources)) — last-emitted wins; (2) disk cleanup at meeting close — after commit phase ends, scan emitted utterances, group by (kind, frozenset(sources)), keep latest, unlink the older files. Safety: only fires when source-list MATCHES EXACTLY (definitionally redundant per Rabbit's semantics). Distinct-but-overlapping sources keep both items (e.g. story-010 + story-011 from this session — different personas, different framings, both keep). See roadmap item 171b36e1 for full design + alternatives.

tasks.title: Auto-transition lifecycle reconciler (artifact-presence-driven)
tasks.details:
Deferred from P12 — described originally as 'background watcher that auto-transitions features based on artifact presence: proposed → in_progress on first impl artifact; in_progress → ready_for_review on (every ticket implemented + tests pass + M6 verdict approve). No auto past ready_for_review — operator gate strict. Layers on top of T87's explicit workflow-level transitions.'

T87 (shipped) is meeting-driven — fires on phase COMPLETE outcome via transition_iteration_to / transition_emitted_to YAML fields. T91 is artifact-presence-driven — scans .wonderland/<artifact-dirs>/ and proposes transitions independent of meeting completion.

Cases T87 misses that T91 catches:
1. Meeting aborts mid-iteration (MEETING_BUDGET / TIMEOUT). Implementation file landed before abort, but feature stays at prior state because outcome wasn't COMPLETE.
2. Operator manually drops files into src/ outside any meeting.
3. Cross-run resumption: implementations on disk from prior run whose M8 never completed. Features stuck at in_progress.
4. Partial run recovery: some lanes finished M8, others budget-capped mid-M7. Features stuck at in_progress.

Pipeline mode (commit 156e76e) makes partial runs more common — one lane completes while another aborts. T91's value lights up when partial-run recovery starts mattering, which is what cross-run iteration is.

Implementation shape: ~150-200 LoC. New reconcile_lifecycle() function called periodically (or on dashboard open / at run start). Scans implementations/, reviews/, tickets/ and proposes lifecycle transitions via feature_lifecycle.transition(). Read-only file scan + lifecycle write. No agent involvement.

tasks.title: API error visibility in telemetry + live-watch banner
tasks.details:
Today's '$0 meetings' diagnosis was that out-of-credits → API errors → agent.py speak() catches the exception and treats as silence → quiescence → meetings 'complete' at $0. Graceful degradation but operator-invisible: from the dashboard, API down looks identical to 'team converged with nothing to add.'

Two-part fix:
1. Telemetry records API errors (currently they land in stderr only). Add error_count + last_error_message fields to TokenTelemetry; agent.py's speak() exception handler reports through the existing on_token_usage callback (or a new on_error callback).
2. Live-watch screen surfaces a banner when error rate is non-zero. Subtle when 1 error (transient retry); prominent when error rate >50% over recent window (probably API down or credit out).

Optional follow-up: per-error-type categorization. 401/insufficient credits is different from 429/rate-limit is different from 500/server error. Each suggests a different operator action (refill credits, wait, retry later).

tasks.title: ProjectContext.process_model field + Cat constitutional clause
tasks.details:
Close the Cat-Flask-service drift class that surfaced in obol's keeper run. Cat's ADR led with 'TUI client' (the directive-as-seed fix landed) but committed to 'TUI client / lightweight backend split' with a REST service in the middle — every keypress crosses an HTTP boundary on localhost. The Tweedles' implementation built the Flask service even though the actual TUI imports backend.py directly (the service is unused).

ProjectContext today has 'runtime: tui' which Cat read as 'the user-facing thing is a TUI' while keeping a hybrid architecture. Add process_model: single | client-server | distributed as a separately authoritative field. 'runtime: tui, process_model: single' closes the door explicitly.

Two complementary changes:
1. Schema: ProjectStack gains process_model field. Skeleton manifests populate it (python-tui = single, fullstack-fastapi-react = client-server, etc.). Render shows 'Process model: single' in the seeded body.
2. Cat's constitution gets a clause: 'Architectural decisions that introduce a deployment boundary (separate processes, network calls, IPC) within a project whose process_model is single MUST be confirmed via question_to_operator before locking in. The deployment shape is operator-bounded; ADRs that drift it require explicit operator authorization.'

The constitutional clause leverages the operator-question pipeline (commit 2cdb3c8 + 716448e) — Cat asks 'should this be split into client+server, or stay single-process?' before shipping the ADR. Operator gets click-to-submit options ('Stay single-process' / 'Split for v2 plumbing' / 'Both, document why').

tasks.title: Distinguish replay from live runs in the live-watch UI
tasks.details:
From the prior obol session: when meetings showed 'complete · $0' across the board, one diagnostic hypothesis was 'maybe the operator launched a replay (MockTurtle) instead of a live run.' That hypothesis turned out wrong (it was the API credit issue), but the underlying confusion is real: live-watch consumes both LiveRunHandle (real, costs money) and MockTurtleHandle (replay, $0) interchangeably. There's no visual signal distinguishing the two.

Add a [REPLAY] badge or color treatment to the live-watch screen header when consuming a MockTurtleHandle. Status bar showing 'replay · 5x speed · src=run-20260510T085719' so the operator can tell at a glance which mode they're in.

Small but high-leverage UX: the diagnosis-confusion class (was that meeting really at $0, or am I watching a snapshot?) shows up enough that prevention is cheaper than re-asking each time.

tasks.title: Phased-path lifecycle dispatch fix
tasks.details: Phased dispatch branch in _run_one_meeting bypassed both transition_emitted_to (per-utterance) and transition_iteration_to (post-MeetingEnd), since both lived inside _convene_one. Symptom: M3 + M5 silently skipped despite upstream meetings shipping artifacts; features stuck at no-state or proposed depending on which transition was missing. Fix: hoisted transition_emitted_to to per-utterance and mirrored both hooks into the phased branch. Caught by live-debugging two obol2 design passes.
tasks.resolution: Two-commit fix (1546581 + 2aa46b3) on top of 112b0a4. Per-utterance transition_emitted_to + post-MeetingEnd transition_iteration_to now both fire on the phased dispatch path. Regression tests added in tests/test_workflow_lifecycle.py::TestEmissionHookFiresInEventLoop covering convene + phased + iteration paths. Operator-visible: M3 stops skipping with '(no items)' on cross-run design passes; M5 picks up M3-decomposed features. Lesson: dispatch asymmetry between _convene_one and run_phased_meeting is a recurring failure shape — when adding behavior post-meeting, mirror into both branches. Released as 0.3.3 (transition_emitted_to portion); transition_iteration_to portion will ship in next patch.
